## Summary
- Rule available since: `v2.6.8`
- Diagnostic Category: [`lint/nursery/noVueDeprecatedFilter`](/reference/diagnostics#diagnostic-category)
- This rule doesn't have a fix.
- The default severity of this rule is [**error**](/reference/diagnostics#error).
- This rule belongs to the following domains:
  - [`vue`](/linter/domains#vue)
- Sources: 
  - Same as [`vue/no-deprecated-filter`](https://eslint.vuejs.org/rules/no-deprecated-filter)

## How to configure
```json title="biome.json"
{
	"linter": {
		"rules": {
			"nursery": {
				"noVueDeprecatedFilter": "error"
			}
		}
	}
}

```
## Description
Disallow the filter syntax that Vue 3 removed.

Vue 2 let you pass a value through a function with a `|` character, as in
`{{ price | currency }}`. This is called a filter. Vue 3 removed filters, so it reads
the `|` as the bitwise OR operator instead. The template still compiles, but the
function is never called, and the page shows a different value.

Call a function instead, for example `{{ currency(price) }}`, or use a
[computed property](https://vuejs.org/guide/essentials/computed.html).

This rule reports a `|` in `{{ }}` and in `v-bind` values, unless it is inside
parentheses, brackets, or braces.

## Examples

### Invalid

```vue
<template>
  <p>{{ price | currency }}</p>
</template>
```

### Valid

```vue
<template>
  <p>{{ currency(price) }}</p>
  <a :title="truncate(capitalize(name), 20)"></a>
  <p>{{ name || "Anonymous" }}</p>
  <p>{{ (flags | mask) }}</p>
</template>
```
